hypothesis: Across single-year age bins, the coefficient of variation of measured stature and of weight is positively associated with the mean annual growth velocity, being lowest where growth decelerates (about ages 8-10) and rising during the adolescent spurt.
pass_criterion: Using NHANES examination-sample data (survey weighted, sex-specific, ages 2-19), for each sex and each of weight and stature, Spearman correlation across age bins between CV(age) and mean annual increment of the mean (age to age+1) is >= +0.6, AND the CV of weight at its adolescent peak (ages 11-15) exceeds the CV at its pre-adolescent minimum (ages 6-10) by at least 15% relative. Pass requires this for weight in both sexes and for stature in at least one sex.
fail_criterion: Spearman correlation between CV and growth velocity < +0.3 for weight in either sex, or no rise in weight CV from the ages 6-10 minimum to the ages 11-15 maximum (relative increase < 5%). Results between these bounds are inconclusive.
interpretation: Thompson's 'coefficient of variability' is the CV (SD/mean x 100) of stature and weight within an age-sex group. 'Rate of growth' is the annual increment in the age-specific mean (cm/yr, kg/yr). Modern reinterpretation: cross-sectional NHANES means stand in for Thompson's longitudinal and school-survey series. Differences in pubertal timing across children inflate the CV during the spurt, a mechanism distinct from Thompson's 'function of rate' but the same observable. The test shows co-variation, not functional causation. Stature CV is small (about 3-6%), so the weight test is primary. Fields used: BMX (BMXWT weight, BMXHT standing height), DEMO (RIAGENDR, RIDAGEYR, exam weights).
